children: is overhauling its breakneck data-center buildout to address reliability problems, potentially slowing one of Elon Musk's biggest long-term growth ambitions.

The company's data-center team is reportedly installing backup systems and cooling equipment before facilities begin operating and conducting far more thorough testing. Previously, those safeguards were added after sites went live, according to The Information. SpaceX is also considering redesigning portions of existing facilities.

The changes follow an outage this month and a management shake-up that brought leaders from SpaceX rocket and Starlink operations into its AI infrastructure team. Musk said the company was taking corrective action to prevent another disruption.
Reliability Could Slow SpaceX's AI Revenue Race

The overhaul may delay capacity additions, but it addresses a fundamental business risk. Customers renting expensive computing infrastructure require dependable power, cooling and backup systems. Faster construction means little if outages interrupt AI training or weaken customer confidence.

SpaceX operates Colossus data centers in Tennessee and Mississippi. Colossus 1 opened in July 2024 after roughly four months of construction, while Colossus 2 began development in March 2025. The company has also explored a Texas expansion and orbital data centers.

The facilities have become an increasingly important source of revenue. SpaceX has rented computing capacity to Anthropic, Alphabet's Google (GOOGL) and Reflection. These contracts help diversify a business that generated $18.7 billion in 2025, mostly from Starlink.

The stakes are enormous. Goldman Sachs previously projected SpaceX's AI-related revenue could climb from $3.2 billion in 2025 to $322 billion by 2030, a 100-fold increase. That forecast also includes Grok and related services.
Investors face a tradeoff. Stronger reliability standards could slow near-term deployment and revenue recognition, but prevent far more costly failures later. The key question is whether SpaceX
can preserve its construction speed while making Colossus infrastructure robust enough for mission-critical AI workloads.

title: SpaceX Hits Troubling Snag in $322 Billion AI Push
